1.text: Now it happened after tha death of Saul, when David was returned from tha slaughter of tha Amalekites, N David had stayed two days in Ziklag;

It came even 2 pass on tha third day, dat, look, a man came out of tha camp from Saul wit his clothes rent, N earth upon his head: N so it was, when he came 2 David, dat he fell 2 tha earth, N did obeisance.
N David said 2 him, From from where come u? N he said 2 him, Out of tha camp of Israel am I escaped.
N David said 2 him, How went tha matter? I pray u, tell me. N he answered, dat tha people r fled from tha battle, N many of tha people also r fallen N dead; N Saul N Jonathan his son r dead also.
N David said 2 tha young man dat told him, How know u dat Saul N Jonathan his son be dead?
N tha young man dat told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, look, Saul leaned upon his spear; N, look, tha chariots N horsemen followed hard after him.
N when he looked behind him, he saw me, N called 2 me. N I answered, Here am I.
N he said 2 me, Who r u? N I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
He said 2 me again, Stand, I pray u, upon me, N kill me: 4 anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.

So I stood upon him, N killed him, because I was sure dat he could not live after dat he was fallen: N I took tha crown dat was upon his head, N tha bracelet dat was on his arm, N have brought ’em here 2 my lord.
Then David took hold on his clothes, N rent ’em; N likewise all tha men dat were wit him:
N dey mourned, N wept, N fasted until even, 4 Saul, N 4 Jonathan his son, N 4 tha people of tha LORD, N 4 tha house of Israel; because dey were fallen by tha sword.
N David said 2 tha young man dat told him, from where r u? N he answered, I am tha son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
N David said 2 him, How were u not afraid 2 stretch forth thine hand 2 destroy tha LORD’s anointed?
N David called one of tha young men, N said, Go near, N fall upon him. N he struck him dat he died.
N David said 2 him, ur blood be upon ur head; 4 ur mouth has testified against u, sayin, I have killed tha LORD’s anointed.
N David lamented wit dis lamentation over Saul N over Jonathan his son:
(Also he told ’em teach tha children of Judah tha use of tha bow: look, it is written in tha book of Jasher.)
Tha beauty of Israel is killed upon ur high places: how r tha mighty fallen!
Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in tha streets of Askelon; lest tha daughters of tha Philistines rejoice, lest tha daughters of tha uncircumcised triumph.

y’all mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, neither let there be rain, upon u, nor fields of offerings: 4 there tha shield of tha mighty is vilely cast away, tha shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed wit oil.
From tha blood of tha killed, from tha fat of tha mighty, tha bow of Jonathan turned not back, N tha sword of Saul returned not empty.
Saul N Jonathan were lovely N pleasant in their lives, N in their death dey were not divided: dey were swifter than eagles, dey were stronger than lions.
y’all daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed u in scarlet, wit other delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon ur clothing.
How r tha mighty fallen in tha midst of tha battle! O Jonathan, u were killed in thine high places.
I am distressed 4 u, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant have u been 2 me: ur love 2 me was wonderful, passing tha love of women.
How r tha mighty fallen, N tha weapons of war perished!

2.text: N it happened after dis, dat David enquired of tha LORD, sayin, Shall I go up in2 any of tha citiez of Judah? N tha LORD said 2 him, Go up. N David said, where shall I go up? N he said, 2 Hebron.
So David went up there, N his two wives also, Ahinoam tha Jezreelitess, N Abigail Nabal’s wife tha Carmelite.
N his men dat were wit him did David bring up, every man wit his household: N dey lived in tha citiez of Hebron.
N tha men of Judah came, N there dey anointed David king over tha house of Judah. N dey told David, sayin, dat tha men of Jabesh-gilead were dey dat buried Saul.
N David sent messengers 2 tha men of Jabesh-gilead, N said 2 ’em, Blessed be y’all of tha LORD, dat y’all have showed dis kindness 2 ur lord, even 2 Saul, N have buried him.
N now tha LORD show kindness N truth 2 u: N I also will requite u dis kindness, because y’all have done dis thing.
Therefore now let ur hands be strengthened, N be y’all valiant: 4 ur master Saul is dead, N also tha house of Judah have anointed me king over ’em.
But Abner tha son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, took Ish-bosheth tha son of Saul, N brought him over 2 Mahanaim;
N made him king over Gilead, N over tha Ashurites, N over Jezreel, N over Ephraim, N over Benjamin, N over all Israel.
Ish-bosheth Saul’s son was forty years old when he began 2 reign over Israel, N reigned two years. But tha house of Judah followed David.
N tha time dat David was king in Hebron over tha house of Judah was seven years N six months.
N Abner tha son of Ner, N tha servants of Ish-bosheth tha son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim 2 Gibeon.
N Joab tha son of Zeruiah, N tha servants of David, went out, N met together by tha pool of Gibeon: N dey sat down, tha one on tha one side of tha pool, N tha other on tha other side of tha pool.
N Abner said 2 Joab, Let tha young men now arise, N play before us. N Joab said, Let ’em arise.
Then there arose N went over by number twelve of Benjamin, which pertained 2 Ish-bosheth tha son of Saul, N twelve of tha servants of David.
N dey caught every one his fellow by tha head, N thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so dey fell down together: so dat place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
N there was a very sore battle dat day; N Abner was beaten, N tha men of Israel, before tha servants of David.
N there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, N Abishai, N Asahel: N Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.
N Asahel pursued after Abner; N in goin he turned not 2 tha right hand nor 2 tha left from followin Abner.
Then Abner looked behind him, N said, r u Asahel? N he answered, I am.
N Abner said 2 him, Turn u aside 2 ur right hand or 2 ur left, N lay u hold on one of tha young men, N take u his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from followin of him.
N Abner said again 2 Asahel, Turn u aside from followin me: so should I strike u 2 tha ground? how then should I hold up my face 2 Joab ur brother?

But he refused 2 turn aside: so Abner wit tha hinder end of tha spear struck him under tha fifth rib, dat tha spear came out behind him; N he fell down there, N died in tha same place: N it happened, dat as many as came 2 tha place where Asahel fell down N died stood still.
Joab also N Abishai pursued after Abner: N tha sun went down when dey were come 2 tha hill of Ammah, dat lies before Giah by tha way of tha wilderness of Gibeon.
N tha children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, N became one troop, N stood on tha top of an hill.

Then Abner called 2 Joab, N said, Shall tha sword devour 4 ever? know u not dat it will be bitterness in tha latter end? how long shall it be then, ere u bid tha people return from followin their brothers?
N Joab said, As God lives, unless u had spoken, surely then in tha morning tha people had gone up every one from followin his brother.
So Joab blew a trumpet, N all tha people stood still, N pursued after Israel no more, neither fought dey any more.
N Abner N his men walked all dat night through tha plain, N passed over Jordan, N went through all Bithron, N dey came 2 Mahanaim.
N Joab returned from followin Abner: N when he had gathered all tha people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen men N Asahel.
But tha servants of David had struck of Benjamin, N of Abner’s men, so dat three hundred N threescore men died.
N dey took up Asahel, N buried him in tha sepulchre of his father, which was in Beth-lehem. N Joab N his men went all night, N dey came 2 Hebron at break of day.

3.text: Now there was long war between tha house of Saul N tha house of David: but David grew stronger N stronger, N tha house of Saul grew weaker N weaker.
N 2 David were sons born in Hebron: N his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam tha Jezreelitess;
N his second, Chileab, of Abigail tha wife of Nabal tha Carmelite; N tha third, Absalom tha son of Maacah tha daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
N tha fourth, Adonijah tha son of Haggith; N tha fifth, Shephatiah tha son of Abital;
N tha sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David’s wife. dese were born 2 David in Hebron.
N it happened, while there was war between tha house of Saul N tha house of David, dat Abner made himself strong 4 tha house of Saul.
N Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, tha daughter of Aiah: N Ish-bosheth said 2 Abner, so have u gone in 2 my father’s concubine?

Then was Abner very angry 4 tha words of Ish-bosheth, N said, Am I a dog’s head, which against Judah do show kindness dis day 2 tha house of Saul ur father, 2 his brothers, N 2 his friends, N have not delivered u in2 tha hand of David, dat u chargest me 2 day wit a fault concerning dis woman?
So do God 2 Abner, N more also, except, as tha LORD has sworn 2 David, even so I do 2 him;
2 translate tha kingdom from tha house of Saul, N 2 set up tha throne of David over Israel N over Judah, from Dan even 2 Beer-sheba.
N he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.
N Abner sent messengers 2 David on his behalf, sayin, Whose is tha land? sayin also, Make ur league wit me, N, look, my hand shall be wit u, 2 bring about all Israel 2 u.
N he said, Well; I will make a league wit u: but one thing I require of u, dat is, u will not see my face, except u first bring Michal Saul’s daughter, when u come 2 see my face.
N David sent messengers 2 Ish-bosheth Saul’s son, sayin, Deliver me my wife Michal, which I espoused 2 me 4 an hundred foreskins of tha Philistines.
N Ish-bosheth sent, N took her from her husband, even from Phaltiel tha son of Laish.
N her husband went wit her along weepin behind her 2 Bahurim. Then said Abner 2 him, Go, return. N he returned.
N Abner had communication wit tha elders of Israel, sayin, y’all sought 4 David in times past 2 be king over u:
Now then do it: 4 tha LORD has spoken of David, sayin, By tha hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of tha hand of tha Philistines, N out of tha hand of all their opps.
N Abner also spoke in tha ears of Benjamin: N Abner went also 2 speak in tha ears of David in Hebron all dat seemed good 2 Israel, N dat seemed good 2 tha whole house of Benjamin.
So Abner came 2 David 2 Hebron, N twenty men wit him. N David made Abner N tha men dat were wit him a feast.

N Abner said 2 David, I will arise N go, N will gather all Israel 2 my lord tha king, dat dey may make a league wit u, N dat u may reign over all dat thine heart desires. N David sent Abner away; N he went in peace.
N, look, tha servants of David N Joab came from pursuing a troop, N brought in a great spoil wit ’em: but Abner was not wit David in Hebron; 4 he had sent him away, N he was gone in peace.
When Joab N all tha host dat was wit him were come, dey told Joab, sayin, Abner tha son of Ner came 2 tha king, N he has sent him away, N he is gone in peace.
Then Joab came 2 tha king, N said, What have u done? look, Abner came 2 u; why is it dat u have sent him away, N he is quite gone?
u know Abner tha son of Ner, dat he came 2 deceive u, N 2 know ur goin out N ur comin in, N 2 know all dat u do.
N when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, which brought him again from tha well of Sirah: but David knew it not.
N when Abner was returned 2 Hebron, Joab took him aside in tha gate 2 speak wit him quietly, N struck him there under tha fifth rib, dat he died, 4 tha blood of Asahel his brother.
N afterward when David heard it, he said, I N my kingdom r guiltless before tha LORD 4 ever from tha blood of Abner tha son of Ner:

Let it rest on tha head of Joab, N on all his father’s house; N let there not fail from tha house of Joab one dat has an issue, or dat is a leper, or dat leaneth on a staff, or dat falls on tha sword, or dat lacketh bread.
So Joab N Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel at Gibeon in tha battle.
N David said 2 Joab, N 2 all tha people dat were wit him, Rend ur clothes, N gird u wit sackcloth, N mourn before Abner. N king David himself followed tha bier.
N dey buried Abner in Hebron: N tha king raised his voice, N wept at tha grave of Abner; N all tha people wept.
N tha king lamented over Abner, N said, Died Abner as a fool dies?
Ur hands were not bound, nor ur feet put in2 fetters: as a man falls before wicked men, so fellest u. N all tha people wept again over him.
N when all tha people came 2 cause David 2 eat food while it was yet day, David sware, sayin, So do God 2 me, N more also, if I taste bread, or ought else, till tha sun be down.
N all tha people took notice of it, N it pleased ’em: as whatever tha king did pleased all tha people.
4 all tha people N all Israel understood dat day dat it was not of tha king 2 kill Abner tha son of Ner.
N tha king said 2 his servants, Know y’all not dat there is a prince N a great man fallen dis day in Israel?
N I am dis day weak, though anointed king; N dese men tha sons of Zeruiah be too hard 4 me: tha LORD shall reward tha doer of evil according 2 his wickedness.

4.text: N when Saul’s son heard dat Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, N all tha Israelites were troubled.

N Saul’s son had two men dat were captains of bands: tha name of tha one was Baanah, N tha name of tha other Rechab, tha sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of tha children of Benjamin: (4 Beeroth also was reckoned 2 Benjamin:
N tha Beerothites fled 2 Gittaim, N were sojourners there until dis day.)

N Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son dat was lame of his feet. He was five years old when tha tidings came of Saul N Jonathan out of Jezreel, N his nurse took him up, N fled: N it happened, as she made haste 2 flee, dat he fell, N became lame. N his name was Mephibosheth.
N tha sons of Rimmon tha Beerothite, Rechab N Baanah, went, N came about tha heat of tha day 2 tha house of Ish-bosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.
N dey came there in2 tha midst of tha house, as though dey would have fetched wheat; N dey struck him under tha fifth rib: N Rechab N Baanah his brother escaped.
4 when dey came in2 tha house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, N dey struck him, N killed him, N beheaded him, N took his head, N got ’em away through tha plain all night.

N dey brought tha head of Ish-bosheth 2 David 2 Hebron, N said 2 tha king, look tha head of Ish-bosheth tha son of Saul thine opp, which sought ur life; N tha LORD has avenged my lord tha king dis day of Saul, N of his seed.
N David answered Rechab N Baanah his brother, tha sons of Rimmon tha Beerothite, N said 2 ’em, As tha LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
When one told me, sayin, look, Saul is dead, thinkin 2 have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, N killed him in Ziklag, who thought dat I would have given him a reward 4 his tidings:
How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of ur hand, N take u away from tha earth?

N David commanded his young men, N dey killed ’em, N cut off their hands N their feet, N hanged ’em up over tha pool in Hebron. But dey took tha head of Ish-bosheth, N buried it in tha sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.

5.text: Then came all tha tribes of Israel 2 David 2 Hebron, N spoke, sayin, look, we r ur bone N ur flesh.
Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, u were he dat leddest out N brought in Israel: N tha LORD said 2 u, u will feed my people Israel, N u will be a captain over Israel.
So all tha elders of Israel came 2 tha king 2 Hebron; N king David made a league wit ’em in Hebron before tha LORD: N dey anointed David king over Israel.
David was thirty years old when he began 2 reign, N he reigned forty years.
In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years N six months: N in Jerusalem he reigned thirty N three years over all Israel N Judah.

N tha king N his men went 2 Jerusalem 2 tha Jebusites, tha inhabitants of tha land: which spoke 2 David, sayin, Except u take away tha blind N tha lame, u will not come in here: thinkin, David cannot come in here.
Nevertheless David took tha strong hold of Zion: tha same is tha city of David.

N David said on dat day, whoever gets up 2 tha gutter, N strikes tha Jebusites, N tha lame N tha blind, dat r hated of David’s soul, he shall be chief N captain. so dey said, tha blind N tha lame shall not come in2 tha house.
So David lived in tha fort, N called it tha city of David. N David built round about from Millo N inward.
N David went on, N grew great, N tha LORD God of hosts was wit him.
N Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers 2 David, N cedar trees, N carpenters, N masons: N dey built David an house.
N David perceived dat tha LORD had established him king over Israel, N dat he had exalted his kingdom 4 his people Israel’s sake.
N David took him more concubines N wives out of Jerusalem, after he was come from Hebron: N there were yet sons N daughters born 2 David.
N dese be tha namez of dose dat were born 2 him in Jerusalem; Shammua, N Shobab, N Nathan, N Solomon,
Ibhar also, N Elishua, N Nepheg, N Japhia,
N Elishama, N Eliada, N Eliphalet.
But when tha Philistines heard dat dey had anointed David king over Israel, all tha Philistines came up 2 seek David; N David heard of it, N went down 2 tha hold.
Tha Philistines also came N spread themselves in tha valley of Rephaim.
N David enquired of tha LORD, sayin, Shall I go up 2 tha Philistines? will u deliver ’em in2 mine hand? N tha LORD said 2 David, Go up: 4 I will doubtless deliver tha Philistines in2 thine hand.
N David came 2 Baal-perazim, N David struck ’em there, N said, tha LORD has broken forth upon mine opps before me, as tha breach of waterz. Therefore he called tha name of dat place Baal-perazim.
N there dey left their images, N David N his men burned ’em.
N tha Philistines came up yet again, N spread themselves in tha valley of Rephaim.
N when David enquired of tha LORD, he said, u will not go up; but fetch a compass behind ’em, N come upon ’em over against tha mulberry trees.
N let it be, when u hear tha sound of a goin in tha tops of tha mulberry trees, dat then u will bestir urself: 4 then shall tha LORD go out before u, 2 strike tha host of tha Philistines.
N David did so, as tha LORD had commanded him; N struck tha Philistines from Geba until u come 2 Gazer.

6.text: Again, David gathered together all tha chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

N David arose, N went wit all tha people dat were wit him from Baale of Judah, 2 bring up from thence tha ark of God, whose name is called by tha name of tha LORD of hosts dat lives between tha cherubims. of hosts, was called upon
N dey set tha ark of God upon a new cart, N brought it out of tha house of Abinadab dat was in Gibeah: N Uzzah N Ahio, tha sons of Abinadab, drave tha new cart.
N dey brought it out of tha house of Abinadab which was at Gibeah, accompanying tha ark of God: N Ahio went before tha ark.
N David N all tha house of Israel played before tha LORD on all manner of instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, N on psalteries, N on timbrels, N on cornets, N on cymbals.
N when dey came 2 Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand 2 tha ark of God, N took hold of it; 4 tha oxen shook it.
N tha anger of tha LORD was kindled against Uzzah; N God struck him there 4 his error; N there he died by tha ark of God.
N David was displeased, because tha LORD had made a breach upon Uzzah: N he called tha name of tha place Perez-uzzah 2 dis day.
N David was afraid of tha LORD dat day, N said, How shall tha ark of tha LORD come 2 me?
So David would not remove tha ark of tha LORD 2 him in2 tha city of David: but David carried it aside in2 tha house of Obed-edom tha Gittite.
N tha ark of tha LORD continued in tha house of Obed-edom tha Gittite three months: N tha LORD blessed Obed-edom, N all his household.

N it was told king David, sayin, tha LORD has blessed tha house of Obed-edom, N all dat pertains 2 him, because of tha ark of God. So David went N brought up tha ark of God from tha house of Obed-edom in2 tha city of David wit gladness.
N it was so, dat when dey dat bare tha ark of tha LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen N fatlings.
N David danced before tha LORD wit all his might; N David was girded wit a linen ephod.
So David N all tha house of Israel brought up tha ark of tha LORD wit shouting, N wit tha sound of tha trumpet.
N as tha ark of tha LORD came in2 tha city of David, Michal Saul’s daughter looked through a window, N saw king David leaping N dancing before tha LORD; N she despised him in her heart.
N dey brought in tha ark of tha LORD, N set it in his place, in tha midst of tha tabernacle dat David had pitched 4 it: N David offered burnt offerings N peace offerings before tha LORD.
N as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings N peace offerings, he blessed tha people in tha name of tha LORD of hosts.

N he dealt among all tha people, even among tha whole crowd of Israel, as well 2 tha women as men, 2 every one a cake of bread, N a good piece of flesh, N a flagon of wine. So all tha people departed every one 2 his house.

Then David returned 2 bless his household. N Michal tha daughter of Saul came out 2 meet David, N said, How glorious was tha king of Israel 2 day, who uncovered himself 2 day in tha eyes of tha handmaids of his servants, as one of tha vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!

N David said 2 Michal, It was before tha LORD, which chose me before ur father, N before all his house, 2 appoint me ruler over tha people of tha LORD, over Israel: therefore will I play before tha LORD.
N I will yet be more vile than like dis, N will be base in my own sight: N of tha maidservants which u have spoken of, of ’em shall I be had in honour.
Therefore Michal tha daughter of Saul had no child 2 tha day of her death.

7.text: N it happened, when tha king sat in his house, N tha LORD had given him rest round about from all his opps;
Dat tha king said 2 Nathan tha prophet, See now, I live in an house of cedar, but tha ark of God lives within curtains.
N Nathan said 2 tha king, Go, do all dat is in thine heart; 4 tha LORD is wit u.
N it happened dat night, dat tha word of tha LORD came 2 Nathan, sayin,
Go N tell my servant David, like dis says tha LORD, will u build me an house 4 me 2 live in?
Whereas I have not lived in any house since tha time dat I brought up tha children of Israel out of Egypt, even 2 dis day, but have walked in a tent N in a tabernacle.

In all tha places in which I have walked wit all tha children of Israel spoke I a word wit any of tha tribes of Israel, whom I commanded 2 feed my people Israel, sayin, Why build y’all not me an house of cedar?
Now therefore so will u say 2 my servant David, like dis says tha LORD of hosts, I took u from tha sheepcote, from followin tha sheep, 2 be ruler over my people, over Israel:
N I was wit u wherever u went, N have cut off all thine opps out of ur sight, N have made u a great name, like 2 tha name of tha great men dat r in tha earth.

Moreover I will appoint a place 4 my people Israel, N will plant ’em, dat dey may live in a place of their own, N move no more; neither shall tha children of wickedness afflict ’em any more, as beforetime,
N as since tha time dat I commanded judges 2 be over my people Israel, N have caused u 2 rest from all thine opps. Also tha LORD tells u dat he will make u an house.
N when ur days be fulfilled, N u will sleep wit ur fathers, I will set up ur seed after u, which shall proceed out of ur bowels, N I will establish his kingdom.
He shall build an house 4 my name, N I will stablish tha throne of his kingdom 4 ever.
I will be his father, N he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him wit tha rod of men, N wit tha stripes of tha children of men:
But my mercy shall not depart away from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before u.
N thine house N ur kingdom shall be established 4 ever before u: ur throne shall be established 4 ever.
According 2 all dese words, N according 2 all dis vision, so did Nathan speak 2 David.
Then went king David in, N sat before tha LORD, N he said, Who am I, O Lord GOD? N what is my house, dat u have brought me until now?
N dis was yet a small thing in ur sight, O Lord GOD; but u have spoken also of ur servant’s house 4 a great while 2 come. N is dis tha manner of man, O Lord GOD?
N what can David say more 2 u? 4 u, Lord GOD, know ur servant.
4 ur word’s sake, N according 2 ur own heart, have u done all dese great things, 2 make ur servant know ’em.
So u r great, O LORD God: 4 there is none like u, neither is there any God beside u, according 2 all dat we have heard wit our ears.

N what one nation in tha earth is like ur people, even like Israel, whom God went 2 redeem 4 a people 2 himself, N 2 make him a name, N 2 do 4 u great things N terrible, 4 ur land, before ur people, which u redeemedst 2 u from Egypt, from tha nations N their gods?
4 u have confirmed 2 urself ur people Israel 2 be a people 2 u 4 ever: N u, LORD, art become their God.
N now, O LORD God, tha word dat u have spoken concerning ur servant, N concerning his house, establish it 4 ever, N do as u have said.
N let ur name be magnified 4 ever, sayin, tha LORD of hosts is tha God over Israel: N let tha house of ur servant David be established before u.
4 u, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed 2 ur servant, sayin, I will build u an house: therefore has ur servant found in his heart 2 pray dis prayer 2 u.
N now, O Lord GOD, u r dat God, N ur words be true, N u have promised dis goodness 2 ur servant:
Therefore now let it please u 2 bless tha house of ur servant, dat it may continue 4 ever before u: 4 u, O Lord GOD, have spoken it: N wit ur blessing let tha house of ur servant be blessed 4 ever.

8.text: N after dis it happened, dat David struck tha Philistines, N subdued ’em: N David took Metheg-ammah out of tha hand of tha Philistines.

N he struck Moab, N measured ’em wit a line, castin ’em down 2 tha ground; even wit two lines measured he 2 put 2 death, N wit one full line 2 keep alive. N so tha Moabites became David’s servants, N brought gifts.
David struck also Hadadezer, tha son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went 2 recover his border at tha river Euphrates.
N David took from him a thousand chariots, N seven hundred horsemen, N twenty thousand footmen: N David houghed all tha chariot horses, but reserved of ’em 4 an hundred chariots.
N when tha Syrians of Damascus came 2 succour Hadadezer king of Zobah, David killed of tha Syrians two N twenty thousand men.
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: N tha Syrians became servants 2 David, N brought gifts. N tha LORD preserved David wherever he went.
N David took tha shields of gold dat were on tha servants of Hadadezer, N brought ’em 2 Jerusalem.
N from Betah, N from Berothai, citiez of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.
When Toi king of Hamath heard dat David had struck all tha host of Hadadezer,

Then Toi sent Joram his son 2 king David, 2 greet him, N 2 bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, N struck him: 4 Hadadezer had wars wit Toi. N Joram brought wit him vessels of silver, N vessels of gold, N vessels of brass:
Which also king David did dedicate 2 tha LORD, wit tha silver N gold dat he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;
Of Syria, N of Moab, N of tha children of Ammon, N of tha Philistines, N of Amalek, N of tha spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
N David got him a name when he returned from strikin of tha Syrians in tha valley of salt, bein eighteen thousand men.
N he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, N all dey of Edom became David’s servants. N tha LORD preserved David wherever he went.
N David reigned over all Israel; N David executed judgment N justice 2 all his people.
N Joab tha son of Zeruiah was over tha host; N Jehoshaphat tha son of Ahilud was recorder;
N Zadok tha son of Ahitub, N Ahimelech tha son of Abiathar, were tha priests; N Seraiah was tha scribe;
N Benaiah tha son of Jehoiada was over both tha Cherethites N tha Pelethites; N David’s sons were chief rulers.

9.text: N David said, Is there yet any dat is left of tha house of Saul, dat I may show him kindness 4 Jonathan’s sake?
N there was of tha house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. N when dey had called him 2 David, tha king said 2 him, r u Ziba? N he said, ur servant is he.
N tha king said, Is there not yet any of tha house of Saul, dat I may show tha kindness of God 2 him? N Ziba said 2 tha king, Jonathan has yet a son, which is lame on his feet.
N tha king said 2 him, Where is he? N Ziba said 2 tha king, look, he is in tha house of Machir, tha son of Ammiel, in look-debar.
Then king David sent, N fetched him out of tha house of Machir, tha son of Ammiel, from look-debar.
Now when Mephibosheth, tha son of Jonathan, tha son of Saul, was come 2 David, he fell on his face, N did reverence. N David said, Mephibosheth. N he answered, look ur servant!
N David said 2 him, don’t fear: 4 I will surely show u kindness 4 Jonathan ur father’s sake, N will restore u all tha land of Saul ur father; N u will eat bread at my table continually.
N he bowed himself, N said, What is ur servant, dat u should look upon such a dead dog as I am?
Then tha king called 2 Ziba, Saul’s servant, N said 2 him, I have given 2 ur master’s son all dat pertained 2 Saul N 2 all his house.

u therefore, N ur sons, N ur servants, shall till tha land 4 him, N u will bring in tha fruits, dat ur master’s son may have food 2 eat: but Mephibosheth ur master’s son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons N twenty servants.

Then said Ziba 2 tha king, According 2 all dat my lord tha king has commanded his servant, so shall ur servant do. As 4 Mephibosheth, said tha king, he shall eat at my table, as one of tha king’s sons.
N Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micha. N all dat lived in tha house of Ziba were servants 2 Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem: 4 he did eat continually at tha king’s table; N was lame on both his feet.

10.text: N it happened after dis, dat tha king of tha children of Ammon died, N Hanun his son reigned in his stead.

Then said David, I will show kindness 2 Hanun tha son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness 2 me. N David sent 2 comfort him by tha hand of his servants 4 his father. N David’s servants came in2 tha land of tha children of Ammon.

N tha princes of tha children of Ammon said 2 Hanun their lord, think u dat David does honour ur father, dat he has sent comforters 2 u? has not David rather sent his servants 2 u, 2 search tha city, N 2 spy it out, N 2 overthrow it?
So Hanun took David’s servants, N shaved off tha one half of their beards, N cut off their garments in tha middle, even 2 their buttocks, N sent ’em away.
When dey told it 2 David, he sent 2 meet ’em, because tha men were greatly ashamed: N tha king said, Tarry at Jericho until ur beards be grown, N then return.

N when tha children of Ammon saw dat dey stank before David, tha children of Ammon sent N hired tha Syrians of Beth-rehob, N tha Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, N of king Maacah a thousand men, N of Ish-tob twelve thousand men.
N when David heard of it, he sent Joab, N all tha host of tha mighty men.
N tha children of Ammon came out, N put tha battle in array at tha entering in of tha gate: N tha Syrians of Zoba, N of Rehob, N Ish-tob, N Maacah, were by themselves in tha field.
When Joab saw dat tha front of tha battle was against him before N behind, he chose of all tha choice men of Israel, N put ’em in array against tha Syrians:
N tha rest of tha people he delivered in2 tha hand of Abishai his brother, dat he might put ’em in array against tha children of Ammon.
N he said, If tha Syrians be too strong 4 me, then u will help me: but if tha children of Ammon be too strong 4 u, then I will come N help u.
Be of good courage, N let us play tha men 4 our people, N 4 tha citiez of our God: N tha LORD do dat which seems him good.
N Joab drew nigh, N tha people dat were wit him, 2 tha battle against tha Syrians: N dey fled before him.
N when tha children of Ammon saw dat tha Syrians were fled, then fled dey also before Abishai, N entered in2 tha city. So Joab returned from tha children of Ammon, N came 2 Jerusalem.
N when tha Syrians saw dat dey were struck before Israel, dey gathered themselves together.
N Hadarezer sent, N brought out tha Syrians dat were beyond tha river: N dey came 2 Helam; N Shobach tha captain of tha host of Hadarezer went before ’em.
N when it was told David, he gathered all Israel together, N passed over Jordan, N came 2 Helam. N tha Syrians set themselves in array against David, N fought wit him.
N tha Syrians fled before Israel; N David killed tha men of seven hundred chariots of tha Syrians, N forty thousand horsemen, N struck Shobach tha captain of their host, who died there.
N when all tha kings dat were servants 2 Hadarezer saw dat dey were struck before Israel, dey made peace wit Israel, N served ’em. So tha Syrians feared 2 help tha children of Ammon any more.

11.text: N it happened, after tha year was expired, at tha time when kings go forth 2 battle, dat David sent Joab, N his servants wit him, N all Israel; N dey destroyed tha children of Ammon, N besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.

N it happened in an eveningtide, dat David arose from off his bed, N walked upon tha roof of tha king’s house: N from tha roof he saw a woman washing herself; N tha woman was very beautiful 2 look upon.
N David sent N enquired after tha woman. N one said, Is not dis Bath-sheba, tha daughter of Eliam, tha wife of Uriah tha Hittite?
N David sent messengers, N took her; N she came in 2 him, N he lay wit her; 4 she was purified from her uncleanness: N she returned 2 her house.
N tha woman conceived, N sent N told David, N said, I am wit child.
N David sent 2 Joab, sayin, Send me Uriah tha Hittite. N Joab sent Uriah 2 David.
N when Uriah was come 2 him, David demanded of him how Joab did, N how tha people did, N how tha war prospered.
N David said 2 Uriah, Go down 2 ur house, N wash ur feet. N Uriah departed out of tha king’s house, N there followed him a mess of food from tha king.
But Uriah slept at tha door of tha king’s house wit all tha servants of his lord, N went not down 2 his house.
N when dey had told David, sayin, Uriah went not down 2 his house, David said 2 Uriah, came u not from ur journey? why then did u not go down 2 thine house?

N Uriah said 2 David, tha ark, N Israel, N Judah, abide in tents; N my lord Joab, N tha servants of my lord, r encamped in tha open fields; shall I then go in2 mine house, 2 eat N 2 drink, N 2 lie wit my wife? as u live, N as ur soul lives, I will not do dis thing.
N David said 2 Uriah, Tarry here 2 day also, N 2 morrow I will let u depart. So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem dat day, N tha morrow.
N when David had called him, he did eat N drink before him; N he made him drunk: N at even he went out 2 lie on his bed wit tha servants of his lord, but went not down 2 his house.
N it happened in tha morning, dat David wrote a letter 2 Joab, N sent it by tha hand of Uriah.
N he wrote in tha letter, sayin, Set y’all Uriah in tha forefront of tha hottest battle, N retire y’all from him, dat he may be struck, N die.
N it happened, when Joab observed tha city, dat he assigned Uriah 2 a place where he knew dat valiant men were.
N tha men of tha city went out, N fought wit Joab: N there fell some of tha people of tha servants of David; N Uriah tha Hittite died also.
Then Joab sent N told David all tha things concerning tha war;
N charged tha messenger, sayin, When u have made an end of telling tha matters of tha war 2 tha king,
N if so be dat tha king’s wrath arise, N he say 2 u, so approached y’all so nigh 2 tha city when y’all did fight? knew y’all not dat dey would shoot from tha wall?

Who struck Abimelech tha son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from tha wall, dat he died in Thebez? why went y’all nigh tha wall? then say u, ur servant Uriah tha Hittite is dead also.
So tha messenger went, N came N showed David all dat Joab had sent him 4.
N tha messenger said 2 David, Surely tha men prevailed against us, N came out 2 us in2 tha field, N we were upon ’em even 2 tha entering of tha gate.
N tha shooters shot from off tha wall upon ur servants; N some of tha king’s servants be dead, N ur servant Uriah tha Hittite is dead also.

Then David said 2 tha messenger, like dis will u say 2 Joab, don’t let dis thing displease u, 4 tha sword devours one as well as another: make ur battle more strong against tha city, N overthrow it: N encourage u him.
N when tha wife of Uriah heard dat Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned 4 her husband.
N when tha mournin was past, David sent N fetched her 2 his house, N she became his wife, N bare him a son. But tha thing dat David had done displeased tha LORD.

12.text: N tha LORD sent Nathan 2 David. N he came 2 him, N said 2 him, There were two men in one city; tha one rich, N tha other poor.
Tha rich man had exceeding many flocks N herds:

But tha poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought N nourished up: N it grew up together wit him, N wit his children; it did eat of his own food, N drank of his own cup, N lay in his bosom, N was 2 him as a daughter.

N there came a traveller 2 tha rich man, N he spared 2 take of his own flock N of his own herd, 2 dress 4 tha wayfaring man dat was come 2 him; but took tha poor man’s lamb, N dressed it 4 tha man dat was come 2 him.
N David’s anger was greatly kindled against tha man; N he said 2 Nathan, As tha LORD lives, tha man dat has done dis thing shall surely die:
N he shall restore tha lamb fourfold, because he did dis thing, N because he had no pity.
N Nathan said 2 David, u r tha man. like dis says tha LORD God of Israel, I anointed u king over Israel, N I delivered u out of tha hand of Saul;
N I gave u ur master’s house, N ur master’s wives in2 ur bosom, N gave u tha house of Israel N of Judah; N if dat had been too little, I would moreover have given 2 u such N such things.

So have u despised tha commandment of tha LORD, 2 do evil in his sight? u have killed Uriah tha Hittite wit tha sword, N have taken his wife 2 be ur wife, N have killed him wit tha sword of tha children of Ammon.
Now therefore tha sword shall never depart from thine house; because u have despised me, N have taken tha wife of Uriah tha Hittite 2 be ur wife.

Like dis says tha LORD, look, I will raise up evil against u out of ur own house, N I will take ur wives before ur eyes, N give ’em 2 ur neighbour, N he shall lie wit ur wives in tha sight of dis sun.
4 u did it secretly: but I will do dis thing before all Israel, N before tha sun.
N David said 2 Nathan, I have sinned against tha LORD. N Nathan said 2 David, tha LORD also has put away ur sin; u will not die.
But, because by dis deed u have given great occasion 2 tha opps of tha LORD 2 blaspheme, tha child also dat is born 2 u shall surely die.
N Nathan departed 2 his house. N tha LORD struck tha child dat Uriah’s wife bare 2 David, N it was very sick.
David therefore besought God 4 tha child; N David fasted, N went in, N lay all night upon tha earth.
N tha elders of his house arose, N went 2 him, 2 raise him up from tha earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread wit ’em.

N it happened on tha seventh day, dat tha child died. N tha servants of David feared 2 tell him dat tha child was dead: 4 dey said, look, while tha child was yet alive, we spoke 2 him, N he would not listen 2 our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him dat tha child is dead?
But when David saw dat his servants whispered, David perceived dat tha child was dead: therefore David said 2 his servants, Is tha child dead? N dey said, He is dead.

Then David arose from tha earth, N washed, N anointed himself, N changed his clothing, N came in2 tha house of tha LORD, N worshipped: then he came 2 his own house; N when he required, dey set bread before him, N he did eat.
Then said his servants 2 him, What thing is dis dat u have done? u did fast N weep 4 tha child, while it was alive; but when tha child was dead, u did rise N eat bread.
N he said, While tha child was yet alive, I fasted N wept: 4 I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious 2 me, dat tha child may live?
But now he is dead, so should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go 2 him, but he shall not return 2 me.
N David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, N went in 2 her, N lay wit her: N she bare a son, N he called his name Solomon: N tha LORD loved him.
N he sent by tha hand of Nathan tha prophet; N he called his name Jedidiah, because of tha LORD.
N Joab fought against Rabbah of tha children of Ammon, N took tha royal city.
N Joab sent messengers 2 David, N said, I have fought against Rabbah, N have taken tha city of waterz.
Now therefore gather tha rest of tha people together, N encamp against tha city, N take it: lest I take tha city, N it be called after my name.
N David gathered all tha people together, N went 2 Rabbah, N fought against it, N took it.

N he took their king’s crown from off his head, tha weight whereof was a talent of gold wit tha precious stones: N it was set on David’s head. N he brought forth tha spoil of tha city in great abundance.

N he brought forth tha people dat were in it, N put ’em under saws, N under harrows of iron, N under axes of iron, N made ’em pass through tha brickkiln: N like dis did he 2 all tha citiez of tha children of Ammon. So David N all tha people returned 2 Jerusalem.

13.text: N it happened after dis, dat Absalom tha son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; N Amnon tha son of David loved her.
N Amnon was so vexed, dat he fell sick 4 his sister Tamar; 4 she was a virgin; N Amnon thought it hard 4 him 2 do any thing 2 her.
But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, tha son of Shimeah David’s brother: N Jonadab was a very subtil man.
N he said 2 him, Why r u, bein tha king’s son, lean from day 2 day? will u not tell me? N Amnon said 2 him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.

N Jonadab said 2 him, Lay u down on ur bed, N make urself sick: N when ur father comes 2 see u, say 2 him, I pray u, let my sister Tamar come, N give me food, N dress tha food in my sight, dat I may see it, N eat it at her hand.

So Amnon lay down, N made himself sick: N when tha king was come 2 see him, Amnon said 2 tha king, I pray u, let Tamar my sister come, N make me a couple of cakes in my sight, dat I may eat at her hand.
Then David sent home 2 Tamar, sayin, Go now 2 ur brother Amnon’s house, N dress him food.
So Tamar went 2 her brother Amnon’s house; N he was laid down. N she took flour, N kneaded it, N made cakes in his sight, N did bake tha cakes.
N she took a pan, N poured ’em out before him; but he refused 2 eat. N Amnon said, Have out all men from me. N dey went out every man from him.
N Amnon said 2 Tamar, Bring tha food in2 tha chamber, dat I may eat of thine hand. N Tamar took tha cakes which she had made, N brought ’em in2 tha chamber 2 Amnon her brother.
N when she had brought ’em 2 him 2 eat, he took hold of her, N said 2 her, Come lie wit me, my sister.
N she answered him, no, my brother, do not force me; 4 no such thing ought 2 be done in Israel: do not u dis folly.
N I, where shall I cause my shame 2 go? N as 4 u, u will be as one of tha fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray u, speak 2 tha king; 4 he will not withhold me from u.
But he would not listen 2 her voice: but, bein stronger than she, forced her, N lay wit her.
Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so dat tha hatred wherewith he hated her was greater than tha love wherewith he had loved her. N Amnon said 2 her, Arise, be gone.
N she said 2 him, There is no cause: dis evil in sending me away is greater than tha other dat u did 2 me. But he would not listen 2 her.
Then he called his servant dat ministered 2 him, N said, Put now dis woman out from me, N bolt tha door after her.
N she had a garment of divers colours upon her: 4 wit such robes were tha king’s daughters dat were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, N bolted tha door after her.
N Tamar put ashes on her head, N rent her garment of divers colours dat was on her, N laid her hand on her head, N went on cryin.
N Absalom her brother said 2 her, has Amnon ur brother been wit u? but hold now ur peace, my sister: he is ur brother; regard not dis thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.
But when king David heard of all dese things, he was very angry.
N Absalom spoke 2 his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: 4 Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
N it happened after two full years, dat Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Ephraim: N Absalom invited all tha king’s sons.
N Absalom came 2 tha king, N said, look now, ur servant has sheepshearers; let tha king, I beg u, N his servants go wit ur servant.
N tha king said 2 Absalom, no, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable 2 u. N he pressed him: but he would not go, but blessed him.
Then said Absalom, If not, I pray u, let my brother Amnon go wit us. N tha king said 2 him, Why should he go wit u?
But Absalom pressed him, dat he let Amnon N all tha king’s sons go wit him.

Now Absalom had commanded his servants, sayin, Mark y’all now when Amnon’s heart is merry wit wine, N when I say 2 u, strike Amnon; then kill him, don’t fear: have not I commanded u? be courageous, N be valiant.
N tha servants of Absalom did 2 Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all tha king’s sons arose, N every man got him up upon his mule, N fled.
N it happened, while dey were in tha way, dat tidings came 2 David, sayin, Absalom has killed all tha king’s sons, N there is not one of ’em left.
Then tha king arose, N tare his garments, N lay on tha earth; N all his servants stood by wit their clothes rent.

N Jonadab, tha son of Shimeah David’s brother, answered, don’t let my lord suppose dat dey have killed all tha young men tha king’s sons; 4 Amnon only is dead: 4 by tha appointment of Absalom dis has been determined from tha day dat he forced his sister Tamar.
Now therefore don’t let my lord tha king take tha thing 2 his heart, 2 think dat all tha king’s sons r dead: 4 Amnon only is dead.
But Absalom fled. N tha young man dat kept tha watch lifted up his eyes, N looked, N, look, there came much people by tha way of tha hill side behind him.
N Jonadab said 2 tha king, look, tha king’s sons come: as ur servant said, so it is.
N it happened, as soon as he had made an end of speakin, dat, look, tha king’s sons came, N lifted up their voice N wept: N tha king also N all his servants wept very sore.
But Absalom fled, N went 2 Talmai, tha son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. N David mourned 4 his son every day.
So Absalom fled, N went 2 Geshur, N was there three years.
N tha soul of king David longed 2 go forth 2 Absalom: 4 he was comforted concerning Amnon, seein he was dead.

14.text: Now Joab tha son of Zeruiah perceived dat tha king’s heart was toward Absalom.

N Joab sent 2 Tekoah, N fetched thence a wise woman, N said 2 her, I pray u, feign urself 2 be a mourner, N put on now mournin clothing, N anoint not urself wit oil, but be as a woman dat had a long time mourned 4 tha dead:
N come 2 tha king, N speak on dis manner 2 him. So Joab put tha words in her mouth.
N when tha woman of Tekoah spoke 2 tha king, she fell on her face 2 tha ground, N did obeisance, N said, Help, O king.
N tha king said 2 her, What ails u? N she answered, I am indeed a widow woman, N mine husband is dead.
N ur handmaid had two sons, N dey two strove together in tha field, N there was none 2 part ’em, but tha one struck tha other, N killed him.

N, look, tha whole family is risen against thine handmaid, N dey said, Deliver him dat struck his brother, dat we may kill him, 4 tha life of his brother whom he killed; N we will destroy tha heir also: N so dey shall quench my coal which is left, N shall not leave 2 my husband neither name nor remainder upon tha earth.
N tha king said 2 tha woman, Go 2 thine house, N I will give charge concerning u.
N tha woman of Tekoah said 2 tha king, My lord, O king, tha iniquity be on me, N on my father’s house: N tha king N his throne be guiltless.
N tha king said, whoever says ought 2 u, bring him 2 me, N he shall not touch u any more.

Then said she, I pray u, let tha king remember tha LORD ur God, dat u would not suffer tha revengers of blood 2 destroy any more, lest dey destroy my son. N he said, As tha LORD lives, there shall not one hair of ur son fall 2 tha earth.
Then tha woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray u, speak one word 2 my lord tha king. N he said, Say on.
N tha woman said, so then have u thought such a thing against tha people of God? 4 tha king does speak dis thing as one which is faulty, in dat tha king does not fetch home again his banished.
4 we must needs die, N r as water spilt on tha ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither does God respect any person: yet does he devise means, dat his banished don’t be expelled from him.

Now therefore dat I am come 2 speak of dis thing 2 my lord tha king, it is because tha people have made me afraid: N ur handmaid said, I will now speak 2 tha king; it may be dat tha king will perform tha request of his handmaid.
4 tha king will hear, 2 deliver his handmaid out of tha hand of tha man dat would destroy me N my son together out of tha inheritance of God.
Then thine handmaid said, tha word of my lord tha king shall now be comfortable: 4 as an angel of God, so is my lord tha king 2 discern good N bad: therefore tha LORD ur God will be wit u.
Then tha king answered 2 tha woman, Hide not from me, I pray u, tha thing dat I shall ask u. N tha woman said, Let my lord tha king now speak.

N tha king said, Is not tha hand of Joab wit u in all dis? N tha woman answered, As ur soul lives, my lord tha king, none can turn 2 tha right hand or 2 tha left from ought dat my lord tha king has spoken: 4 ur servant Joab, he told me, N he put all dese words in tha mouth of thine handmaid:
2 fetch about dis form of speech has ur servant Joab done dis thing: N my lord is wise, according 2 tha wisdom of an angel of God, 2 know all things dat r in tha earth.
N tha king said 2 Joab, look now, I have done dis thing: go therefore, bring tha young man Absalom again.

N Joab fell 2 tha ground on his face, N bowed himself, N thanked tha king: N Joab said, 2 day ur servant knows dat I have found grace in ur sight, my lord, O king, in dat tha king has fulfilled tha request of his servant.
So Joab arose N went 2 Geshur, N brought Absalom 2 Jerusalem.
N tha king said, Let him turn 2 his own house, N let him not see my face. So Absalom returned 2 his own house, N saw not tha king’s face.
But in all Israel there was none 2 be so much praised as Absalom 4 his beauty: from tha sole of his foot even 2 tha crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

N when he polled his head, (4 it was at every year’s end dat he polled it: because tha hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed tha hair of his head at two hundred shekels after tha king’s weight.
N 2 Absalom there were born three sons, N one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.
So Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, N saw not tha king’s face.
Therefore Absalom sent 4 Joab, 2 have sent him 2 tha king; but he would not come 2 him: N when he sent again tha second time, he would not come.
Therefore he said 2 his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, N he has barley there; go N set it on fire. N Absalom’s servants set tha field on fire.
Then Joab arose, N came 2 Absalom 2 his house, N said 2 him, so have ur servants set my field on fire?

N Absalom answered Joab, look, I sent 2 u, sayin, Come here, dat I may send u 2 tha king, 2 say, so am I come from Geshur? it had been good 4 me 2 have been there still: now therefore let me see tha king’s face; N if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me.
So Joab came 2 tha king, N told him: N when he had called 4 Absalom, he came 2 tha king, N bowed himself on his face 2 tha ground before tha king: N tha king kissed Absalom.

15.text: N it happened after dis, dat Absalom prepared him chariots N horses, N fifty men 2 run before him.

N Absalom rose up early, N stood beside tha way of tha gate: N it was so, dat when any man dat had a controversy came 2 tha king 4 judgment, then Absalom called 2 him, N said, Of what city r u? N he said, ur servant is of one of tha tribes of Israel.
N Absalom said 2 him, See, ur matters r good N right; but there is no man deputed of tha king 2 hear u.
Absalom said moreover, Oh dat I were made judge in tha land, dat every man which has any suit or cause might come 2 me, N I would do him justice!
N it was so, dat when any man came nigh 2 him 2 do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, N took him, N kissed him.
N on dis manner did Absalom 2 all Israel dat came 2 tha king 4 judgment: so Absalom stole tha hearts of tha men of Israel.
N it happened after forty years, dat Absalom said 2 tha king, I pray u, let me go N pay my vow, which I have vowed 2 tha LORD, in Hebron.
4 ur servant vowed a vow while I stayed at Geshur in Syria, sayin, If tha LORD shall bring me again indeed 2 Jerusalem, then I will serve tha LORD.
N tha king said 2 him, Go in peace. So he arose, N went 2 Hebron.
But Absalom sent spies throughout all tha tribes of Israel, sayin, As soon as y’all hear tha sound of tha trumpet, then y’all shall say, Absalom reigns in Hebron.
N wit Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, dat were called; N dey went in their simplicity, N dey knew not any thing.
N Absalom sent 4 Ahithophel tha Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. N tha conspiracy was strong; 4 tha people increased continually wit Absalom.
N there came a messenger 2 David, sayin, tha hearts of tha men of Israel r after Absalom.

N David said 2 all his servants dat were wit him at Jerusalem, Arise, N let us flee; 4 we shall not else escape from Absalom: make speed 2 depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, N bring evil upon us, N strike tha city wit tha edge of tha sword.
N tha king’s servants said 2 tha king, look, ur servants r ready 2 do whatever my lord tha king shall appoint.
N tha king went forth, N all his household after him. N tha king left ten women, which were concubines, 2 keep tha house.
N tha king went forth, N all tha people after him, N tarried in a place dat was far off.
N all his servants passed on beside him; N all tha Cherethites, N all tha Pelethites, N all tha Gittites, six hundred men which came after him from Gath, passed on before tha king.
Then said tha king 2 Ittai tha Gittite, so go u also wit us? return 2 ur place, N abide wit tha king: 4 u r a stranger, N also an exile.
Whereas u came but yesterday, should I dis day make u go up N down wit us? seein I go where I may, return u, N take back ur brothers: mercy N truth be wit u.
N Ittai answered tha king, N said, As tha LORD lives, N as my lord tha king lives, surely in what place my lord tha king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will ur servant be.
N David said 2 Ittai, Go N pass over. N Ittai tha Gittite passed over, N all his men, N all tha little ones dat were wit him.
N all tha country wept wit a loud voice, N all tha people passed over: tha king also himself passed over tha brook Kidron, N all tha people passed over, toward tha way of tha wilderness.
N look Zadok also, N all tha Levites were wit him, bearin tha ark of tha covenant of God: N dey set down tha ark of God; N Abiathar went up, until all tha people had done passing out of tha city.
N tha king said 2 Zadok, Carry back tha ark of God in2 tha city: if I shall find favour in tha eyes of tha LORD, he will bring me again, N show me both it, N his habitation:
But if he like dis say, I have no delight in u; look, here am I, let him do 2 me as seems good 2 him.
Tha king said also 2 Zadok tha priest, Art not u a seer? return in2 tha city in peace, N ur two sons wit u, Ahimaaz ur son, N Jonathan tha son of Abiathar.
See, I will tarry in tha plain of tha wilderness, until there come word from u 2 certify me.
Zadok therefore N Abiathar carried tha ark of God again 2 Jerusalem: N dey tarried there.

N David went up by tha ascent of mount Olivet, N wept as he went up, N had his head covered, N he went barefoot: N all tha people dat was wit him covered every man his head, N dey went up, weepin as dey went up.
N one told David, sayin, Ahithophel is among tha conspirators wit Absalom. N David said, O LORD, I pray u, turn tha counsel of Ahithophel in2 foolishness.
N it happened, dat when David was come 2 tha top of tha mount, where he worshipped God, look, Hushai tha Archite came 2 meet him wit his coat rent, N earth upon his head:
2 whom David said, If u pass on wit me, then u will be a burden 2 me:

But if u return 2 tha city, N say 2 Absalom, I will be ur servant, O king; as I have been ur father’s servant until now, so will I now also be ur servant: then may u 4 me defeat tha counsel of Ahithophel.
N have u not there wit u Zadok N Abiathar tha priests? therefore it shall be, dat what thing soever u will hear out of tha king’s house, u will tell it 2 Zadok N Abiathar tha priests.
Look, dey have there wit ’em their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok’s son, N Jonathan Abiathar’s son; N by ’em y’all shall send 2 me every thing dat y’all can hear.
So Hushai David’s friend came in2 tha city, N Absalom came in2 Jerusalem.

16.text: N when David was a little past tha top of tha hill, look, Ziba tha servant of Mephibosheth met him, wit a couple of asses saddled, N upon ’em two hundred loaves of bread, N an hundred bunches of raisins, N an hundred of summer fruits, N a bottle of wine.

N tha king said 2 Ziba, What mean u by dese? N Ziba said, tha asses be 4 tha king’s household 2 ride on; N tha bread N summer fruit 4 tha young men 2 eat; N tha wine, dat such as be faint in tha wilderness may drink.
N tha king said, N where is ur master’s son? N Ziba said 2 tha king, look, he abides at Jerusalem: 4 he said, 2 day shall tha house of Israel restore me tha kingdom of my father.
Then said tha king 2 Ziba, look, thine r all dat pertained 2 Mephibosheth. N Ziba said, I humbly beg u dat I may find grace in ur sight, my lord, O king.
N when king David came 2 Bahurim, look, thence came out a man of tha family of tha house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, tha son of Gera: he came forth, N cursed still as he came.
N he cast stones at David, N at all tha servants of king David: N all tha people N all tha mighty men were on his right hand N on his left.
N like dis said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, u bloody man, N u man of Belial:

Tha LORD has returned upon u all tha blood of tha house of Saul, in whose stead u have reigned; N tha LORD has delivered tha kingdom in2 tha hand of Absalom ur son: N, look, u r taken in ur mischief, because u r a bloody man.
Then said Abishai tha son of Zeruiah 2 tha king, Why should dis dead dog curse my lord tha king? let me go over, I pray u, N take off his head.
N tha king said, What have I 2 do wit u, y’all sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because tha LORD has said 2 him, Curse David. Who shall then say, so have u done so?

N David said 2 Abishai, N 2 all his servants, look, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeks my life: how much more now may dis Benjamite do it? let him alone, N let him curse; 4 tha LORD has bidden him.
It may be dat tha LORD will look on mine affliction, N dat tha LORD will requite me good 4 his cursing dis day.
N as David N his men went by tha way, Shimei went along on tha hill’s side over against him, N cursed as he went, N threw stones at him, N cast dust.
N tha king, N all tha people dat were wit him, came weary, N refreshed themselves there.
N Absalom, N all tha people tha men of Israel, came 2 Jerusalem, N Ahithophel wit him.
N it happened, when Hushai tha Archite, David’s friend, was come 2 Absalom, dat Hushai said 2 Absalom, God save tha king, God save tha king.
N Absalom said 2 Hushai, Is dis ur kindness 2 ur friend? why went u not wit ur friend?
N Hushai said 2 Absalom, no; but whom tha LORD, N dis people, N all tha men of Israel, choose, his will I be, N wit him will I abide.
N again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in tha presence of his son? as I have served in ur father’s presence, so will I be in ur presence.
Then said Absalom 2 Ahithophel, Give counsel among u what we shall do.

N Ahithophel said 2 Absalom, Go in 2 ur father’s concubines, which he has left 2 keep tha house; N all Israel shall hear dat u r abhorred of ur father: then shall tha hands of all dat r wit u be strong.
So dey spread Absalom a tent upon tha top of tha house; N Absalom went in 2 his father’s concubines in tha sight of all Israel.
N tha counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in dose days, was as if a man had enquired at tha oracle of God: so was all tha counsel of Ahithophel both wit David N wit Absalom.

17.text: Moreover Ahithophel said 2 Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, N I will arise N pursue after David dis night:
N I will come upon him while he is weary N weak handed, N will make him afraid: N all tha people dat r wit him shall flee; N I will strike tha king only:
N I will bring back all tha people 2 u: tha man whom u seek is as if all returned: so all tha people shall be in peace.
N tha sayin pleased Absalom well, N all tha elders of Israel.
Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai tha Archite also, N let us hear likewise what he says.
N when Hushai was come 2 Absalom, Absalom spoke 2 him, sayin, Ahithophel has spoken after dis manner: shall we do after his sayin? if not; speak u.
N Hushai said 2 Absalom, tha counsel dat Ahithophel has given is not good at dis time.

4, said Hushai, u know ur father N his men, dat dey be mighty men, N dey be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in tha field: N ur father is a man of war, N will not lodge wit tha people.

Look, he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: N it will come 2 pass, when some of ’em be overthrown at tha first, dat whoever hears it will say, There is a slaughter among tha people dat follow Absalom.
N he also dat is valiant, whose heart is as tha heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: 4 all Israel knows dat ur father is a mighty man, N dey which be wit him r valiant men.
Therefore I counsel dat all Israel be generally gathered 2 u, from Dan even 2 Beer-sheba, as tha sand dat is by tha sea 4 crowd; N dat u go 2 battle in ur own person.

So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, N we will light upon him as tha dew falls on tha ground: N of him N of all tha men dat r wit him there shall not be left so much as one.
Moreover, if he be got in2 a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes 2 dat city, N we will draw it in2 tha river, until there don’t be one small stone found there.

N Absalom N all tha men of Israel said, tha counsel of Hushai tha Archite is better than tha counsel of Ahithophel. 4 tha LORD had appointed 2 defeat tha good counsel of Ahithophel, 2 tha intent dat tha LORD might bring evil upon Absalom.
Then said Hushai 2 Zadok N 2 Abiathar tha priests, like dis N like dis did Ahithophel counsel Absalom N tha elders of Israel; N like dis N like dis have I counselled.
Now therefore send quickly, N tell David, sayin, Lodge not dis night in tha plains of tha wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest tha king be swallowed up, N all tha people dat r wit him.
Now Jonathan N Ahimaaz stayed by En-rogel; 4 dey might not be seen 2 come in2 tha city: N a wench went N told ’em; N dey went N told king David.
Nevertheless a lad saw ’em, N told Absalom: but dey went both of ’em away quickly, N came 2 a man’s house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; where dey went down.
N tha woman took N spread a covering over tha well’s mouth, N spread ground corn thereon; N tha thing was not known.

N when Absalom’s servants came 2 tha woman 2 tha house, dey said, Where is Ahimaaz N Jonathan? N tha woman said 2 ’em, dey be gone over tha brook of water. N when dey had sought N could not find ’em, dey returned 2 Jerusalem.

N it happened, after dey were departed, dat dey came up out of tha well, N went N told king David, N said 2 David, Arise, N pass quickly over tha water: 4 like dis has Ahithophel counselled against u.
Then David arose, N all tha people dat were wit him, N dey passed over Jordan: by tha morning light there lacked not one of ’em dat was not gone over Jordan.

N when Ahithophel saw dat his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, N arose, N got him home 2 his house, 2 his city, N put his household in order, N hanged himself, N died, N was buried in tha sepulchre of his father.
Then David came 2 Mahanaim. N Absalom passed over Jordan, he N all tha men of Israel wit him.
N Absalom made Amasa captain of tha host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man’s son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite, dat went in 2 Abigail tha daughter of Nahash, sister 2 Zeruiah Joab’s mother.
So Israel N Absalom pitched in tha land of Gilead.
N it happened, when David was come 2 Mahanaim, dat Shobi tha son of Nahash of Rabbah of tha children of Ammon, N Machir tha son of Ammiel of look-debar, N Barzillai tha Gileadite of Rogelim,
Brought beds, N basons, N earthen vessels, N wheat, N barley, N flour, N parched corn, N beans, N lentiles, N parched pulse,
N honey, N butter, N sheep, N cheese of kine, 4 David, N 4 tha people dat were wit him, 2 eat: 4 dey said, tha people is hungry, N weary, N thirsty, in tha wilderness.

18.text: N David numbered tha people dat were wit him, N set captains of thousands N captains of hundreds over ’em.

N David sent forth a third part of tha people under tha hand of Joab, N a third part under tha hand of Abishai tha son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, N a third part under tha hand of Ittai tha Gittite. N tha king said 2 tha people, I will surely go forth wit u myself also.

But tha people answered, u will not go forth: 4 if we flee away, dey will not care 4 us; neither if half of us die, will dey care 4 us: but now u r worth ten thousand of us: therefore now it is better dat u succour us out of tha city.
N tha king said 2 ’em, What seems u best I will do. N tha king stood by tha gate side, N all tha people came out by hundreds N by thousands.
N tha king commanded Joab N Abishai N Ittai, sayin, Deal gently 4 my sake wit tha young man, even wit Absalom. N all tha people heard when tha king gave all tha captains charge concerning Absalom.
So tha people went out in2 tha field against Israel: N tha battle was in tha wood of Ephraim;
Where tha people of Israel were killed before tha servants of David, N there was there a great slaughter dat day of twenty thousand men.
4 tha battle was there scattered over tha face of all tha country: N tha wood devoured more people dat day than tha sword devoured.

N Absalom met tha servants of David. N Absalom rode upon a mule, N tha mule went under tha thick boughs of a great oak, N his head caught hold of tha oak, N he was taken up between tha heaven N tha earth; N tha mule dat was under him went away.
N a certain man saw it, N told Joab, N said, look, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
N Joab said 2 tha man dat told him, N, look, u saw him, N why did u not strike him there 2 tha ground? N I would have given u ten shekels of silver, N a girdle.

N tha man said 2 Joab, Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against tha king’s son: 4 in our hearin tha king charged u N Abishai N Ittai, sayin, Beware dat none touch tha young man Absalom.
Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against my own life: 4 there is no matter hid from tha king, N u urself would have set urself against me.
Then said Joab, I may not tarry like dis wit u. N he took three darts in his hand, N thrust ’em through tha heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in tha midst of tha oak.
N ten young men dat bare Joab’s armour compassed about N struck Absalom, N killed him.
N Joab blew tha trumpet, N tha people returned from pursuing after Israel: 4 Joab held back tha people.
N dey took Absalom, N cast him in2 a great pit in tha wood, N laid a very great heap of stones upon him: N all Israel fled every one 2 his tent.

Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken N reared up 4 himself a pillar, which is in tha king’s dale: 4 he said, I have no son 2 keep my name in remembrance: N he called tha pillar after his own name: N it is called 2 dis day, Absalom’s place.
Then said Ahimaaz tha son of Zadok, Let me now run, N bear tha king tidings, how dat tha LORD has avenged him of his opps.
N Joab said 2 him, u will not bear tidings dis day, but u will bear tidings another day: but dis day u will bear no tidings, because tha king’s son is dead.
Then said Joab 2 Cushi, Go tell tha king what u have seen. N Cushi bowed himself 2 Joab, N ran.
Then said Ahimaaz tha son of Zadok yet again 2 Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray u, also run after Cushi. N Joab said, so will u run, my son, seein dat u have no tidings ready?
But howsoever, said he, let me run. N he said 2 him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by tha way of tha plain, N overran Cushi.
N David sat between tha two gates: N tha watchman went up 2 tha roof over tha gate 2 tha wall, N lifted up his eyes, N looked, N look a man runnin alone.
N tha watchman cried, N told tha king. N tha king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. N he came apace, N drew near.
N tha watchman saw another man runnin: N tha watchman called 2 tha porter, N said, look another man runnin alone. N tha king said, He also brings tidings.
N tha watchman said, Me thinks tha runnin of tha foremost is like tha runnin of Ahimaaz tha son of Zadok. N tha king said, He is a good man, N comes wit good tidings.

N Ahimaaz called, N said 2 tha king, All is well. N he fell down 2 tha earth upon his face before tha king, N said, Blessed be tha LORD ur God, which has delivered up tha men dat lifted up their hand against my lord tha king.
N tha king said, Is tha young man Absalom safe? N Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent tha king’s servant, N me ur servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.
N tha king said 2 him, Turn aside, N stand here. N he turned aside, N stood still.
N, look, Cushi came; N Cushi said, Tidings, my lord tha king: 4 tha LORD has avenged u dis day of all ’em dat rose up against u.
N tha king said 2 Cushi, Is tha young man Absalom safe? N Cushi answered, tha opps of my lord tha king, N all dat rise against u 2 do u hurt, be as dat young man is.

N tha king was much moved, N went up 2 tha chamber over tha gate, N wept: N as he went, like dis he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died 4 u, O Absalom, my son, my son!

19.text: N it was told Joab, look, tha king weepeth N mourns 4 Absalom.
N tha victory dat day was turned in2 mournin 2 all tha people: 4 tha people heard say dat day how tha king was grieved 4 his son.
N tha people got ’em by stealth dat day in2 tha city, as people bein ashamed steal away when dey flee in battle.
But tha king covered his face, N tha king cried wit a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!

N Joab came in2 tha house 2 tha king, N said, u have shamed dis day tha faces of all ur servants, which dis day have saved ur life, N tha lives of ur sons N of ur daughters, N tha lives of ur wives, N tha lives of ur concubines;

In dat u love thine opps, N hate ur friends. 4 u have declared dis day, dat u regard neither princes nor servants: 4 dis day I perceive, dat if Absalom had lived, N all we had died dis day, then it had pleased u well.

Now therefore arise, go forth, N speak comfortably 2 ur servants: 4 I swear by tha LORD, if u go not forth, there will not tarry one wit u dis night: N dat will be worse 2 u than all tha evil dat befell u from ur youth until now.
Then tha king arose, N sat in tha gate. N dey told 2 all tha people, sayin, look, tha king does sit in tha gate. N all tha people came before tha king: 4 Israel had fled every man 2 his tent.

N all tha people were at strife throughout all tha tribes of Israel, sayin, tha king saved us out of tha hand of our opps, N he delivered us out of tha hand of tha Philistines; N now he is fled out of tha land 4 Absalom.
N Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak y’all not a word of bringin tha king back?

N king David sent 2 Zadok N 2 Abiathar tha priests, sayin, Speak 2 tha elders of Judah, sayin, Why r y’all tha last 2 bring tha king back 2 his house? seein tha speech of all Israel is come 2 tha king, even 2 his house.
y’all r my brothers, y’all r my bones N my flesh: so then r y’all tha last 2 bring back tha king?
N say y’all 2 Amasa, r u not of my bone, N of my flesh? God do so 2 me, N more also, if u don’t be captain of tha host before me continually in tha room of Joab.
N he bowed tha heart of all tha men of Judah, even as tha heart of one man; so dat dey sent dis word 2 tha king, Return u, N all ur servants.
So tha king returned, N came 2 Jordan. N Judah came 2 Gilgal, 2 go 2 meet tha king, 2 conduct tha king over Jordan.
N Shimei tha son of Gera, a Benjamite, which was of Bahurim, hasted N came down wit tha men of Judah 2 meet king David.
N there were a thousand men of Benjamin wit him, N Ziba tha servant of tha house of Saul, N his fifteen sons N his twenty servants wit him; N dey went over Jordan before tha king.
N there went over a ferry boat 2 carry over tha king’s household, N 2 do what he thought good. N Shimei tha son of Gera fell down before tha king, as he was come over Jordan;

N said 2 tha king, don’t let my lord impute iniquity 2 me, neither do u remember dat which ur servant did perversely tha day dat my lord tha king went out of Jerusalem, dat tha king should take it 2 his heart.
4 ur servant does know dat I have sinned: therefore, look, I am come tha first dis day of all tha house of Joseph 2 go down 2 meet my lord tha king.
But Abishai tha son of Zeruiah answered, Shall not Shimei be put 2 death 4 dis, because he cursed tha LORD’s anointed?

N David said, What have I 2 do wit u, y’all sons of Zeruiah, dat y’all should dis day be adversaries 2 me? shall there any man be put 2 death dis day in Israel? 4 do not I know dat I am dis day king over Israel?
Therefore tha king said 2 Shimei, u will not die. N tha king sware 2 him.

N Mephibosheth tha son of Saul came down 2 meet tha king, N had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from tha day tha king departed until tha day he came again in peace.
N it happened, when he was come 2 Jerusalem 2 meet tha king, dat tha king said 2 him, so went not u wit me, Mephibosheth?
N he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: 4 ur servant said, I will saddle me an ass, dat I may ride thereon, N go 2 tha king; because ur servant is lame.
N he has slandered ur servant 2 my lord tha king; but my lord tha king is as an angel of God: do therefore what is good in ur eyes.
4 all of my father’s house were but dead men before my lord tha king: yet did u set ur servant among ’em dat did eat at ur own table. What right therefore have I yet 2 cry any more 2 tha king?
N tha king said 2 him, Why speak u any more of ur matters? I have said, u N Ziba divide tha land.
N Mephibosheth said 2 tha king, yeah, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord tha king is come again in peace 2 his own house.
N Barzillai tha Gileadite came down from Rogelim, N went over Jordan wit tha king, 2 conduct him over Jordan.
Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: N he had provided tha king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; 4 he was a very great man.
N tha king said 2 Barzillai, Come u over wit me, N I will feed u wit me in Jerusalem.
N Barzillai said 2 tha king, How long have I 2 live, dat I should go up wit tha king 2 Jerusalem?

I am dis day fourscore years old: N can I discern between good N evil? can ur servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more tha voice of singin men N singin women? so then should ur servant be yet a burden 2 my lord tha king?
Ur servant will go a little way over Jordan wit tha king: N why should tha king recompense it me wit such a reward?

Let ur servant, I pray u, turn back again, dat I may die in my own city, N be buried by tha grave of my father N of my mother. But look ur servant Chimham; let him go over wit my lord tha king; N do 2 him what shall seem good 2 u.
N tha king answered, Chimham shall go over wit me, N I will do 2 him dat which shall seem good 2 u: N whatever u will require of me, dat will I do 4 u.
N all tha people went over Jordan. N when tha king was come over, tha king kissed Barzillai, N blessed him; N he returned 2 his own place.
Then tha king went on 2 Gilgal, N Chimham went on wit him: N all tha people of Judah conducted tha king, N also half tha people of Israel.

N, look, all tha men of Israel came 2 tha king, N said 2 tha king, Why have our brothers tha men of Judah stolen u away, N have brought tha king, N his household, N all David’s men wit him, over Jordan?
N all tha men of Judah answered tha men of Israel, Because tha king is near of kin 2 us: so then be y’all angry 4 dis matter? have we eaten at all of tha king’s cost? or has he given us any gift?

N tha men of Israel answered tha men of Judah, N said, We have ten parts in tha king, N we have also more right in David than y’all: why then did y’all despise us, dat our advice should not be first had in bringin back our king? N tha words of tha men of Judah were fiercer than tha words of tha men of Israel.

20.text: N there happened 2 be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, tha son of Bichri, a Benjamite: N he blew a trumpet, N said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in tha son of Jesse: every man 2 his tents, O Israel.
So every man of Israel went up from after David, N followed Sheba tha son of Bichri: but tha men of Judah clave 2 their king, from Jordan even 2 Jerusalem.

N David came 2 his house at Jerusalem; N tha king took tha ten women his concubines, whom he had left 2 keep tha house, N put ’em in ward, N fed ’em, but went not in 2 ’em. So dey were shut up 2 tha day of their death, livin in widowhood.
Then said tha king 2 Amasa, Assemble me tha men of Judah within three days, N be u here present.
So Amasa went 2 assemble tha men of Judah: but he tarried longer than tha set time which he had appointed him.
N David said 2 Abishai, Now shall Sheba tha son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take u ur lord’s servants, N pursue after him, lest he get him fenced citiez, N escape us.
N there went out after him Joab’s men, N tha Cherethites, N tha Pelethites, N all tha mighty men: N dey went out of Jerusalem, 2 pursue after Sheba tha son of Bichri.

When dey were at tha great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa went before ’em. N Joab’s garment dat he had put on was girded 2 him, N upon it a girdle wit a sword fastened upon his loins in tha sheath of it; N as he went forth it fell out.
N Joab said 2 Amasa, r u in health, my brother? N Joab took Amasa by tha beard wit tha right hand 2 kiss him.

But Amasa took no heed 2 tha sword dat was in Joab’s hand: so he struck him wit it in tha fifth rib, N shed out his bowels 2 tha ground, N struck him not again; N he died. So Joab N Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba tha son of Bichri.
N one of Joab’s men stood by him, N said, He dat favoureth Joab, N he dat is 4 David, let him go after Joab.

N Amasa wallowed in blood in tha midst of tha highway. N when tha man saw dat all tha people stood still, he removed Amasa out of tha highway in2 tha field, N cast a cloth upon him, when he saw dat every one dat came by him stood still.

N he went through all tha tribes of Israel 2 Abel, N 2 Beth-maachah, N all tha Berites: N dey were gathered together, N went also after him.
N dey came N besieged him in Abel of Beth-maachah, N dey cast up a bank against tha city, N it stood in tha trench: N all tha people dat were wit Joab battered tha wall, 2 throw it down.

N Joab answered, Far be it, far be it from me, dat I should swallow up or destroy.

Tha matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba tha son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against tha king, even against David: deliver him only, N I will depart from tha city. N tha woman said 2 Joab, look, his head shall be thrown 2 u over tha wall.

Then tha woman went 2 all tha people in her wisdom. N dey cut off tha head of Sheba tha son of Bichri, N cast it out 2 Joab. N he blew a trumpet, N dey retired from tha city, every man 2 his tent. N Joab returned 2 Jerusalem 2 tha king.

21.text: Then there was a famine in tha days of David three years, year after year; N David enquired of tha LORD. N tha LORD answered, It is 4 Saul, N 4 his bloody house, because he killed tha Gibeonites.

N he delivered ’em in2 tha hands of tha Gibeonites, N dey hanged ’em in tha hill before tha LORD: N dey fell all seven together, N were put 2 death in tha days of harvest, in tha first days, in tha beginning of barley harvest.

N Rizpah tha daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, N spread it 4 her upon tha rock, from tha beginning of harvest until water dropped upon ’em out of heaven, N suffered neither tha birds of tha air 2 rest on ’em by day, nor tha beasts of tha field by night.
N it was told David what Rizpah tha daughter of Aiah, tha concubine of Saul, had done.

N David went N took tha bones of Saul N tha bones of Jonathan his son from tha men of Jabesh-gilead, which had stolen ’em from tha street of Beth-shan, where tha Philistines had hanged ’em, when tha Philistines had killed Saul in Gilboa:

22.text: N David spoke 2 tha LORD tha words of dis song in tha day dat tha LORD had delivered him out of tha hand of all his opps, N out of tha hand of Saul:

23.text: Now dese be tha last words of David. David tha son of Jesse said, N tha man who was raised up on high, tha anointed of tha God of Jacob, N tha sweet psalmist of Israel, said,

N Benaiah tha son of Jehoiada, tha son of a valiant man, of Kabzeel, who had done many acts, he killed two lionlike men of Moab: he went down also N killed a lion in tha midst of a pit in time of snow:

24.text: N again tha anger of tha LORD was kindled against Israel, N he moved David against ’em 2 say, Go, number Israel N Judah.
